lead: Pick how the applets and the menu panel move. Every option runs the same scene; click the controls or use the Replay links.

options.name: Fluid springs
options.sub: Springs on real state changes only. Nothing moves on hover or while idle.
rows: What moves
The segmented thumb, the switch knobs, and the tab thumb slide; buttons press to 97 percent; the panel, the applet, and the sheet open; numbers count to the new value on reset.
Timing

Knobs and thumbs use a spring of response 0.30 s and damping 0.80 (390 ms, 1.5 percent overshoot). Sliders on reset use 0.40 s and 0.86. The panel opens in 180 ms and the applet in 200 ms from scale 0.96. The sheet drops with a spring of 0.36 s and 0.84. Reset staggers controls by 18 ms.
Best at
It feels like a native Mac or iOS app: motion starts on the same frame as the click and a second click reverses it from where it is.
Cost
About ten spring values to keep in one motion token file. Each move is one SwiftUI animation on a state change, so the cost at run time is close to zero.

options.name: Quiet
options.sub: Only the essential moves, short and without bounce.
rows: What moves
Thumbs and knobs slide, and the panel, the applet, and the sheet fade with a 4 px move. Buttons do not scale, controls do not stagger, and numbers change at once.
Timing
Every move uses cubic-bezier(0.25, 1, 0.5, 1). Knobs and thumbs take 140 ms, sliders on reset 160 ms, the panel, the applet, and the sheet 160 ms to open and 120 ms to close.
Best at
It is calm and quick. Nobody will call it web-like, and it keeps the spirit of the instant rule.
Cost
The least work after Instant. It can feel a little flat next to Apple apps, because nothing has spring.

options.name: Instant (keep as is)
options.sub: The rule of today: every change happens in one frame.
rows: What moves
Nothing slides or scales. Only the panel open and the sheet keep a 100 ms fade, like the system.
Timing
All controls change in 0 ms. The panel and the sheet fade in and out in 100 ms, linear.
Best at
It is the fastest and it is the rule that ships today, so it needs no work.
Cost
No work. It does not give the premium feel you asked for, and a jump from one state to the next is easy to miss.

options.name: Expressive
options.sub: Fluid springs plus one more layer of motion.
rows: What moves
Everything in Fluid springs. Also the applet sections rise in 30 ms apart, the reset button fills and turns into a check, the color well ripples, and panel pages slide sideways.
Timing

Sections rise 6 px in 280 ms with cubic-bezier(0.2, 0.9, 0.25, 1). The reset fill takes 520 ms and the check shows at 440 ms. The ripple takes 520 ms. Pages slide 24 px with the knob spring; the old page fades out in 100 ms and the new one fades in over 200 ms after 70 ms.
Best at
It is the most premium on the first look and in a demo, and every extra move still follows a real state change.
Cost
It can feel like too much: the section rise on every applet open and the page slide repeat many times a day. The reset fill adds 0.5 s before the check shows.

native.Switch knob, segmented thumb, tab thumb: withAnimation(.spring(response: 0.30, dampingFraction: 0.80)) on the bound value; the selection fill is one view moved with matchedGeometryEffect.
native.Switch knob stretch: A custom ToggleStyle reads configuration.isPressed through a ButtonStyle wrapper and widens the knob by 5 pt with the same spring.
native.Button press: A ButtonStyle with .scaleEffect(configuration.isPressed ? 0.97 : 1) and .animation(.spring(response: 0.26, dampingFraction: 0.62), value: configuration.isPressed).
native.Slider knob while pressed: onEditingChanged sets a pressed flag; .scaleEffect(pressed ? 1.18 : 1) with the press spring.
native.Menu panel open and close: NSPanel animator: NSAnimationContext with duration 0.18 and a CAMediaTimingFunction(controlPoints: 0.2, 0.9, 0.25, 1) on alphaValue, plus a scale of the content layer from 0.96 with the same curve, anchored at the status item.
native.Menu panel resize between pages: Measure the new page, then setFrame(_:display:animate:) inside NSAnimationContext, or SwiftUI .animation(.spring(response: 0.34, dampingFraction: 0.90), value: page) on the content height.
native.Applet window open: NSWindow.animationBehavior = .none, then animate the content layer from scale 0.96 and alpha 0 over 0.20 s (Quiet: alpha only with a 4 pt move).
native.Confirmation sheet: beginSheet keeps the system sheet motion; a SwiftUI .sheet uses the system spring. A custom in-window sheet uses .transition(.move(edge: .top)) with .spring(response: 0.36, dampingFraction: 0.84).
native.Numbers that change on reset: Text(value, format: .number).contentTransition(.numericText(value: value)) inside the same spring as the slider (response 0.40, dampingFraction 0.86).
native.Reset stagger: Apply each control change in its own withAnimation(.spring(...).delay(Double(index) * 0.018)).
native.Expressive extras: Section rise: .transition(.opacity.combined(with: .offset(y: 6))) with .delay(index * 0.03). Page slide: .transition(.push(from: .trailing)). Reset fill: a Rectangle with .scaleEffect(x: progress, anchor: .leading). Ripple: a stroked overlay animated with .easeOut(duration: 0.52).
native.Reduce Motion: Read @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) (AppKit: NSWorkspace.shared.accessibilityDisplayShouldReduceMotion) and use nil animations, keeping only the 100 ms fades.
